title: Benchmarking the Energy Savings with Speculative Decoding Strategies
quote: Vanilla autoregressive decoding, despite higher latency, can sometimes be more energy-efficient than SD approaches (CoGA and DyGA).
proves: Only dedicated SD energy benchmark found: single A5000 24GB, CodeCarbon (pynvml+RAPL), several SD methods incl. EAGLE-3; lower latency does not give proportional energy savings; some SD methods use more total energy than vanilla on Vicuna-13B.
does_not_prove: Batch size 1 only (paper says so); no power cap, no DVFS, no per-phase power; no rejected-token energy split; draft energy share not reported.
bearing: Supports energy-per-token gap at batch>1 and under caps; threatens any claim that SD is always greener

title: Energy Considerations of Large Language Model Inference and Efficiency Optimizations
quote: speculative decoding requiring 25.65% more energy when performing inference at a batch size of 128
proves: SD (gamma=4; Llama-3.1-8B/3.2-1B, R1-Distill-32B/1.5B) cuts total energy up to ~29% at batch<=16 but costs 25.65% more energy at batch 128 on A6000/A100/A6000 Ada.
does_not_prove: Fixed gamma=4, offline batches, no adaptive K, no power cap or clock control, no EAGLE/MTP; mechanism (excess verification) asserted not profiled per phase.
bearing: Establishes energy crossover vs batch size; threatens novelty of 'SD wastes energy at high batch' but leaves energy-optimal K/controller open

title: PELM: Power Efficient On-Device LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling
quote: PELM completed 45% of queries before hitting the limit, while zTT completed only 34%.
proves: Joint DVFS + speculative depth + verification depth governor on Jetson AGX Orin and Orin Nano; up to 52.4% energy reduction and 23.1% speedup; thermally constrained runs where non-thermal-aware methods fail to finish query sets.
does_not_prove: Jetson only (no phone, no Apple silicon, no datacenter GPU); self-speculation/early exit, not EAGLE/draft-model serving; single-request edge, no batching.
bearing: Directly occupies 'SD + DVFS + thermal' on edge; threatens a naive on-device thermal-aware K idea; Apple unified-memory fanless case still open

title: The Illusion of Power Capping in LLM Decode: A Phase-Aware Energy Characterisation Across Attention Architectures
quote: decode draws only 137–300 W on a 700 W GPU
proves: On H200, plain decode is memory-bound and draws 137-300 W so power caps never trigger; SM clock locking Pareto-dominates power capping, recovering up to 32% decode energy; large batch/long context shifts optimum clock up to 1185-1590 MHz.
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding or verification; SD raises arithmetic intensity per step, so whether caps start to bind under SD is untested.
bearing: Supports gap: does SD (compute-heavier verification) make power caps bind and change optimal clock?

title: DynamoLLM: Designing LLM Inference Clusters for Performance and Energy Efficiency
quote: DynamoLLM conserves 53% energy and 38% operational carbon emissions, and reduces 61% cost to the customer,
proves: Cluster-level reconfiguration of instance count, parallelism and GPU frequency saves 53% energy under SLOs.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding in the configuration space; abstract only checked.
bearing: Speculation (on/off, K) is a missing knob in energy-managed clusters

title: throttLL'eM: Predictive GPU Throttling for Energy Efficient LLM Inference Serving
quote: throttLL’eM achieves up to 43.8% lower energy consumption
proves: Iteration-level GPU frequency selection from projected KV usage and batch size; up to 43.8% lower energy vs Triton.
does_not_prove: Lists speculative decoding only in related work; its performance model assumes one token per iteration, unvalidated with SD's variable tokens per step.
bearing: Supports gap: frequency predictors break when tokens per step vary with acceptance

title: POLCA: Power Oversubscription in LLM Cloud Providers
quote: we can deploy 30% more servers in the same GPU cluster for inference, with minimal performance loss.
proves: Inference clusters have power headroom allowing ~30% oversubscription (simulation from production power patterns).
does_not_prove: No SD; whether SD raises per-GPU power (shrinking oversubscription headroom) not studied.
bearing: Capacity-under-power framing; SD power uplift could eat oversubscription headroom

title: Accelerating Mobile Language Model via Speculative Decoding and NPU-Coordinated Execution
quote: SpecInfer suffers from energy overhead amplified by drafter computation.
proves: On Redmi K60 Pro and OnePlus 13 (power via /sys/class/power_supply, 100 ms), SD+NPU gives 1.07-4.71x energy savings; smaller (1.42-1.85x) on Llama3.2 3B; draft compute adds energy overhead.
does_not_prove: RAG workloads, rooted Android only; no sustained thermal runs; no Apple silicon.
bearing: Phone SD energy measured; threatens generic 'on-device SD energy' novelty

title: Lossless but Not Free: An Empirical Anatomy of Speculative Decoding on Consumer Hardware
quote: three of five configurations decelerate.
proves: On an Apple-silicon laptop, best SD config gives 1.61x at K=6; three of five configs slow down; a quantized Metal backend runs parallel verification serially.
does_not_prove: No energy or power measurement; no thermal/sustained runs.
bearing: Supports Mac SD-energy gap; warns SD may slow down on Metal so energy could rise

title: LLM Inference at the Edge: Mobile, NPU, and GPU Performance Efficiency Trade-offs Under Sustained Load
quote: the iPhone 16 Pro loses nearly half its throughput within two iterations
proves: Sustained decode on passively cooled phones: iPhone 16 Pro 40.35 -> 22.56 tok/s (44% drop); S24 Ultra OS terminates after 6 iterations; RTX 4050 sustains 131.7 tok/s at 34.1 W.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding (only suggested as future work); no phone power numbers.
bearing: Supports gap: SD speedup under sustained thermal throttling on fanless devices unmeasured

title: Cross-Family Speculative Decoding for Polish Language Models on Apple Silicon: An Empirical Evaluation of Bielik 11B with UAG-Extended MLX-LM
quote: verification cost on unified memory does not amortize as theory predicts because both models are memory-bandwidth bound
proves: On M2 Pro 32 GB, MLX SD reaches 1.7x only on structured text; energy given only as TDP estimate (~2.0 J/token, 30 W / 15 tok/s).
does_not_prove: Energy is estimated from TDP, not measured; no SD-vs-AR energy comparison; no thermal data.
bearing: Supports Apple SD energy gap; shows unified-memory verification does not amortize

title: GreenLLM: Disaggregating Large Language Model Serving on Heterogeneous GPUs for Lower Carbon Emissions
quote: GreenLLM reduces carbon emissions by up to 40.6% compared to running standard LLM serving on new GPU only.
proves: Reusing older GPUs for parts of serving cuts carbon up to 40.6%; secondary summaries say configs include a speculative split (draft on old GPU).
does_not_prove: Abstract does not mention speculative decoding; spec-decode configuration not verified from the page.
bearing: Carbon-aware placement of drafter on old GPUs partially occupied

title: DeepSeek R1 · Speculative Decoding (GB300 FP4 MTP vs none page)
quote: Points from different engines are not directly comparable on the same curve
proves: At 59 tok/s/user MTP gives 13357 vs 6821 tok/s/GPU ($0.05 vs ~$0.09/M tokens); at 138 tok/s/user 3821 vs 180; also reports tok/s/MW (6.3M vs 3.2M at 59 tok/s/user).
does_not_prove: tok/s/MW appears derived from throughput and nominal power, not measured draw; interpolated, cross-engine; workload label inconsistent (1k/1k vs 8K/1K).
bearing: Fleet capacity: SD roughly doubles per-GPU throughput at moderate interactivity; no measured power under SD

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: the draft models can occupy up to 38∼140% memory footprint of target models
proves: Draft model plus its KV can take 38-140% of target memory at large batch; KV grows linearly with batch; sparse draft KV gives up to 2.51x at batch 32-256 for long context.
does_not_prove: No energy/power; capacity argued in memory, not GPUs provisioned for a load.
bearing: Drafter-memory vs KV capacity tradeoff already studied for long context

title: Where Does the Energy Go? Profiling LLM Agent Inference on Blackwell GPUs
quote: throughput remains unchanged under per-GPU power caps of 400-600 W but drops sharply at 300 W.
proves: Blackwell power-cap sweep 300-600 W: caps above 400 W are inert, 300 W causes sharp drop; agentic sequential workloads use 63x more energy per output token than saturated serving.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding; agent workloads at low batch are exactly where SD is used, but untested.
bearing: Supports gap: SD in low-batch agent serving under power caps

title: Where Do the Joules Go? Diagnosing Inference Energy Consumption
quote: GPU utilization differences can result in 3--5$\times$ energy differences
proves: ML.ENERGY-group study: 46 models, 1,858 configs on H100/B200; task type causes 25x and utilization 3-5x energy differences.
does_not_prove: Does not mention speculative decoding.
bearing: Largest recent energy measurement campaign omits SD; gap

title: Optimized Multi-Token Joint Decoding with Auxiliary Model for LLM Inference
quote: MTAD achieves a 1.42x speed-up and consumes 1.54x less energy than conventional speculative decoding methods.
proves: Measured energy of SD variants; a joint-decoding method uses 1.54x less energy than conventional SD.
does_not_prove: Batch 1 style evaluation; no power caps or serving load.
bearing: Energy as SD design objective exists; threatens 'first energy-aware SD' claims

title: EnerInfer: Energy-Aware On-Device LLM Inference
quote: improves energy efficiency by up to 65%, 12%, and 24% on phones, a laptop, and a development board
proves: NPU/DDR frequency tuning gives up to 65% (phones), 12% (laptop), 24% (dev board) energy efficiency.
does_not_prove: No speculative decoding; laptop model not named in abstract.
bearing: On-device DVFS crowded; SD dimension missing here

title: Characterizing LLM Inference Energy-Performance Tradeoffs across Workloads and GPU Scaling
quote: does not capture production serving dynamics such as continuous batching, speculative decoding, or multi-GPU execution
proves: Decode is clock-insensitive: 2842 -> 180 MHz saves 42% energy with 1-6% latency increase.
does_not_prove: Explicitly excludes speculative decoding; SD verification may not be clock-insensitive.
bearing: Supports gap: optimal clock under SD

title: Splitwise: Efficient generative LLM inference using phase splitting
quote: achieve 2.35x more throughput with the same cost and power budgets
proves: Token generation phase can run on lower-power hardware; 2.35x throughput at same cost and power budget.
does_not_prove: No SD; SD makes decode more compute-heavy, which may undercut the low-power-decode premise.
bearing: Power-budget provisioning baseline without SD

title: GreenLLM: SLO-Aware Dynamic Frequency Scaling for Energy-Efficient LLM Serving
quote: achieves up to 34% reduction in total energy consumption compared to the default DVFS baseline
proves: Separate prefill/decode clock control on A100 with Alibaba/Azure traces: 10-34% energy cut; decode controller tunes SM clock every 20 ms to meet P95 TBT.
does_not_prove: No SD; TBT model assumes one token per decode step.
bearing: Decode DVFS controllers ignore SD; gap

title: vLLM blog post on speculative decoding dated 2024-10-17 (exact title not captured)
quote: The extra compute required to propose and verify tokens can sometimes slow down the system when it is already compute-bound
proves: SD slows Llama3-70B on 4xH100 at high QPS (1.4x slowdown ShareGPT, 1.8x CNN/DM); up to 1.5x (draft) / 2.8x (prompt lookup) speedup at low QPS.
does_not_prove: Throughput only, no energy; old vLLM V0.
bearing: Capacity: SD can reduce serving capacity at high load

title: Speculative Decoding: Exploiting Speculative Execution for Accelerating Seq2seq Generation
quote: while SpecDec’s GPU power consumption is 28% higher, its GPU hours are 540% shorter than autoregressive decoding.
proves: On P100, SpecDec draws 110 W vs 86 W for AR (28% higher) but total energy 6.05 Wh vs 25.54 Wh for 3000 sentences.
does_not_prove: Old seq2seq NAR drafter, P100, batch effects not studied; power is average not per phase.
bearing: Only direct measurement found that SD raises average GPU power; relevant to caps

title: Accelerating PayPal's Commerce Agent with Speculative Decoding: An Empirical Study on EAGLE3 with Fine-Tuned Nemotron Models
quote: speculative decoding on a single H100 matches or exceeds NIM on two H100s, enabling 50% GPU cost reduction.
proves: Production-style provisioning: EAGLE3 gamma=3 gives 22-49% throughput and 18-33% latency gain; 1 H100 with SD matches 2 H100s without.
does_not_prove: Concurrency only 1-32; no energy; one workload.
bearing: Capacity provisioning with SD measured at small scale

title: MemSpec: Memory-Aware Runtime for Adaptive Draft Scheduling in Speculative Decoding on Edge Devices
quote: On memory-constrained edge devices, however, these methods often fail to improve end-to-end throughput
proves: Under tight memory budgets on Jetson Orin Nano, draft switching overhead kills adaptive-draft gains; resident working-set management improves throughput 40.7%.
does_not_prove: No energy/thermal; Jetson not Apple unified memory.
bearing: Edge drafter-memory capacity already occupied

title: Speculation at a Distance: Where Edge-Cloud Speculative Decoding Actually Pays Off
quote: sustain (1 + γ t_d/t_v) times more concurrent clients at the same per-client rate
proves: Analytic capacity result: offloading drafting to clients lets a saturated server serve (1+γ t_d/t_v)x more clients.
does_not_prove: No energy or power; analytic.
bearing: Capacity via drafter offload occupied (and R05 killed similar placement ideas)

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
quote: verification stage generally takes the largest execution time, ranging from 42% to 95% in all execution methods
proves: On H100 vLLM, EAGLE speedup falls 1.73x -> 1.21x from batch 1 to 128 (Llama3.1-8B GSM8K); verification is 42-95% of time; EAGLE drafting <20%.
does_not_prove: No energy or power.
bearing: Verification dominates time, so verification power is the energy lever; gap in per-phase power

title: Energy-Efficient Wireless LLM Inference via Uncertainty and Importance-Aware Speculative Decoding
quote: saving the energy consumption by 40.7% compared to standard HLM.
proves: Device-cloud hybrid SD that skips uploads saves 40.7% energy vs standard hybrid LM.
does_not_prove: Communication energy focus, 0.37 tok/s, not GPU power or thermal.
bearing: Energy-aware SD in wireless setting occupied
